messages:
sam: Heads up — customers flagged quota split again. Root cause looks like inconsistent SDK attribution headers across clients.
ivy: Which shapes are we seeing this time?
sam: Mix of `x-rw-attr: acct=org9` , `X-Redwood-Attribution: {"acct":"org9","route":"beta"}` and legacy `acct_key=org9`.
nate: Interesting: TS started emitting a JSON header for richer context, Python kept a compact string, Go uses token claim. Console creates distinct buckets for each header name/shape.
ivy: We need a short-term mitigation and a longer SDK migration plan. Short-term: Console can present a merged visualization but keep billing data separate. Label it clearly: "merged view (heuristic)".
sam: Agreed. Also add a small adoption metric: percent of requests with canonical header shape. That helps track migration.
nate: For SDKs: propose canonical header: `X-Redwood-Attribution: acct=...;route=...` (textual, semicolon separated). TS & Py should emit both shapes for 2 weeks during rollout. Go should emit a no-op canonical header to match.
ivy: TS middleware change is minimal — add normalization middleware to write canonical header from JSON or legacy fields. I can PR today.
sam: Python owners: we need to flip default to structured emission but keep legacy for a grace period. Add env var to opt-in/out.
nate: Go: no parsing on hot path; write a tiny header with acct only, e.g. `X-Redwood-Attribution: acct=org9` to avoid perf hit.
op-bot: rollout plan logged: console merged-viz canary 2026-05-05T18:00Z 5% -> 25% -> 100% if stable.
ivy: Tests: add synths that send mixed headers and assert console merged count equals sum of raw buckets for viz, and billing invoices still show raw buckets.
sam: Support playbook: how to run curl examples to inspect headers, how to toggle merged view, and an escalation path to SDK owners. I'll draft the blurb.
ivy: I'll open the TS PR: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-ts/pull/531 (middleware + unit tests for mixed-case and both header shapes).
nate: I'll coordinate with go-sdk folks to add the no-op header and include microbenchmarks.
sam: Action items: Ivy (TS PR + tests), Python owners (structured default + flag), Nate (Go shim + perf), Console (merged-viz + adoption metric + labeled tooltip). Recheck in #devex-standup in 36h.
